question.text: Under SEBI regulations, mutual fund schemes must disclose their portfolio holdings to the public at what frequency?

answer.text: Month-end and half-year-end on AMC and AMFI websites within 10 days; debt schemes additionally disclose portfolios fortnightly within 5 days

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series V-A workbook (p110), all mutual fund schemes must disclose their portfolios as on the last day of the month and as on the last day of the half-year on the AMC and AMFI websites, within 10 days of the relevant period. Debt schemes are additionally required to disclose their portfolios on a fortnightly basis, within 5 days from the end of the fortnight. The Trap: Annual and quarterly frequencies understate the current disclosure cycle. Daily disclosure is not the regulatory requirement (NAV is disclosed daily, but portfolios are not). Options that omit either the month-end/half-year-end track or the debt-scheme fortnightly track are incomplete. Note: Two parallel disclosure tracks operate together — the general month-end and half-year-end timelines for all schemes, and the additional fortnightly timeline that applies specifically to debt schemes.
